nodes.title: Make a first investment feel understandable, controlled, and trustworthy
nodes.bodyText:
# Lumen Trade
A fictional, cash-only stock trading app for first-time investors. All names, targets, dates, decisions, and progress are invented demo data.

## Product thesis
People make a confident first investment when identity, funding, market information, and order handling work as one journey. Shared ledger, identity, and event capabilities support multiple customer outcomes.

## Success by 31 March 2027
- Increase verified-to-funded conversion from a fictional 38% baseline to 60%.
- Increase funded-to-first-order conversion from 25% to 45% within seven days.
- Increase four-week retained funded accounts from 20% to 35%.

## Guardrails
No duplicate orders; every cash movement reconciles; show stale quotes; explain risk before confirmation. No margin, options, crypto, or investment recommendations in launch scope.

## Demo route
Explore weighted Themes, platform dependencies, briefs, Questions, Criteria, Gantt, and Forecast. Change the ledger schedule to review downstream impact. Compare a smaller launch scope and added capacity as saved scenarios.

nodes.title: Reusable identity verification and eligibility
nodes.bodyText:
## Customer / platform value
A single verification state gates deposits and orders. Retried callbacks must not create duplicate accounts.

## Scope
Cash-only stocks in a fictional sandbox. All service providers and test accounts are simulated.

## Evidence and outcome
Duplicate verification callbacks produce one customer and one eligibility decision.
Measure through the shared journey-event contract; validate correctness before interpreting conversion.

## Delivery notes
Owner: Avery Chen · Identity & experience. Estimates are illustrative points, not delivery promises.

openQuestions.questionText: Should unsettled deposits be available for trading?
openQuestions.decisionText: No. Launch uses settled cash only; prioritize reconciliation and clear expectations.

openQuestions.questionText: Which stale-quote threshold is understandable in customer testing?
How should a timed-out order confirmation explain an unknown outcome?
Should return-rate experiments include urgency prompts?
openQuestions.decisionText: No. Use opt-in informational alerts; measure comprehension alongside retention.
